section: International environmental treaties - Stockholm 1972, Rio 1992, Ramsar, CITES, CBD and its protocols
subsections: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding CITES:
1. It was adopted on 3 March 1973 at Washington, D.C.
2. It entered into force on 1 July 1975.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Geneva and is administered by UNEP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CITES was adopted on 3 March 1973, entered into force on 1 July 1975, and has a UNEP-administered Secretariat in Geneva.
accepted.tq: Combine date, commencement and institutional-location facts in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the CITES Appendix?
o: Appendix I — trade is controlled only through permits
Appendix II — species are already extinct and cannot be traded
Appendix III — all international trade is prohibited
Appendix I — commercial trade in listed species is generally prohibited
accepted.x: Appendix I covers species threatened with extinction for which commercial trade is generally prohibited.
accepted.tq: Test the precise difference between the three CITES appendices.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to CITES, consider the following statements:
1. Appendix II includes species that are not yet threatened with extinction but whose trade is controlled through permits.
2. Appendix III includes species listed by one Party seeking the assistance of other Parties to control trade.
3. Appendix I consists of species for which commercial trade is permitted without restrictions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Appendix II covers species whose trade requires control and permits, while Appendix III covers species listed by one Party for international assistance. Appendix I generally prohibits commercial trade.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the reversed trade rule.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the 19th Conference of the Parties to CITES held in 2022, which category of species was moved to Appendix II?
accepted.x: CoP19 in 2022 moved 54 shark and ray species to CITES Appendix II.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive numerical figure associated with a treaty decision.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: TRAFFIC is best described as a
o: wildlife-trade monitoring network jointly associated with WWF and IUCN
accepted.x: TRAFFIC is a wildlife-trade monitoring network and a joint programme of WWF and IUCN, established in 1976.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation by its function and institutional association.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding CITES is NOT correct?
o: It regulates international trade in wild fauna and flora.
Commercial trade is prohibited for approximately 97 per cent of the species covered by it.
Parties designate Management Authorities and Scientific Authorities.
accepted.x: CITES prohibits commercial trade for approximately 3 per cent of the species covered and regulates the remaining 97 per cent; the statement reverses these proportions.
accepted.tq: Check the reversed percentage trap in a NOT question.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the implementation of CITES, the Management Authority primarily deals with _____, whereas the Scientific Authority provides _____.
accepted.x: The Management Authority issues or handles permits, while the Scientific Authority provides scientific advice.
accepted.tq: Match institutional functions to the authority responsible for them.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The CITES Trade Database is maintained by
accepted.x: The CITES Trade Database is maintained by the United Nations Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC).
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-body identification method for specialised databases.
accepted.sec: CITES - other name, appendices, secretariat, TRAFFIC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Convention on Migratory Species:
1. It is also called the Bonn Convention.
2. Its Secretariat is located at Bonn under UNEP.
3. India became a Party to it in 1983.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CMS is the Bonn Convention, has its UNEP-linked Secretariat at Bonn, and India has been a Party since 1983.
accepted.tq: Combine alternative name, headquarters and membership-year facts.
accepted.sec: CMS - appendices, COP hosted by India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Convention on Migratory Species, Appendix I comprises migratory species that are
o: endangered and subject to strict protection
listed by one Party for trade regulation
accepted.x: CMS Appendix I contains endangered migratory species requiring strict protection.
accepted.tq: Distinguish CMS appendices from the similarly numbered CITES appendices.
accepted.sec: CMS - appendices, COP hosted by India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes CMS Appendix II?
o: It contains species needing international cooperation agreements for their conservation.
It contains only extinct migratory species.
It contains species listed by one country to control imports.
It prohibits all trade in every listed species.
accepted.x: CMS Appendix II covers migratory species whose conservation requires international cooperation agreements.
accepted.tq: Discriminate CMS Appendix II from CITES Appendix II.
accepted.sec: CMS - appendices, COP hosted by India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India hosted the 13th Conference of Parties to the Convention on Migratory Species at
accepted.x: CMS COP-13 was hosted at Gandhinagar, India, in February 2020.
accepted.tq: Pair the host country, city and year-month without swapping nearby conference details.
accepted.sec: CMS - appendices, COP hosted by India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following groups of species was added to CMS Appendix I at CMS COP-13 hosted by India?
o: Blue whale, dugong and olive ridley turtle
Ganges dolphin, snow leopard and blackbuck
Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican
Tiger, Asiatic lion and one-horned rhinoceros
accepted.x: The Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican were added to CMS Appendix I at COP-13.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact species group attached to a conference decision.
accepted.sec: CMS - appendices, COP hosted by India  [APPSC]

accepted.s: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed on
accepted.x: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed annually on 22 May.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact date of a named international observance.
accepted.sec: Environment days → date  [other exams]

accepted.s: World Environment Day is observed on 5 June because the date is associated with the opening of the
accepted.x: World Environment Day on 5 June commemorates the opening of the Stockholm Conference.
accepted.tq: Connect an observance date with the international event that explains it.
accepted.sec: Environment days → date  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at
accepted.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in Iran.
accepted.tq: Identify the treaty by its adoption place and year.

accepted.s: The Secretariat of the Ramsar Convention is located at
accepted.x: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is located at Gland, Switzerland.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the treaty Secretariat’s location from other environment bodies’ headquarters.

accepted.s: Which was the first Indian site designated under the Ramsar Convention?
accepted.x: Chilika Lake was the first Indian Ramsar site, designated in 1981.
accepted.tq: Use first-in-sequence recall for national treaty-site facts.
accepted.sec: Ramsar Convention - year, obligations, Montreux Record, India's sites, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Chilika Lake was designated as a Ramsar site in
accepted.x: Chilika Lake received Ramsar designation in 1981.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first-site year from later Indian site designations.
accepted.sec: Ramsar Convention - year, obligations, Montreux Record, India's sites, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Ramsar Convention?
o: Udaipur and Indore — India's first accredited Wetland Cities
Chilika and Kolleru — Wetland Cities accredited in 2025
Keoladeo and Loktak — first accredited Wetland Cities
Gland and Ramsar — Indian Wetland Cities
accepted.x: Udaipur and Indore became India's first accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the designation with the correct sites rather than the better-known Ramsar locations.
accepted.sec: Ramsar Convention - year, obligations, Montreux Record, India's sites, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent Ramsar-related developments in India:
1. India's resolution on sustainable lifestyles for wise use of wetlands was adopted at Ramsar COP-15.
2. The resolution was adopted on 30 July 2025.
3. The Amrit Dharohar strategy was launched in June 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the resolution was adopted at COP-15 on 30 July 2025, and the Amrit Dharohar strategy dates to June 2023.
accepted.tq: Use a three-statement chronology-and-event combination.
accepted.sec: Ramsar Convention - year, obligations, Montreux Record, India's sites, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Wetlands Rules, 2017, which of the following provides the domestic legal framework referred to for wetlands?
accepted.x: The Wetlands Rules, 2017 constitute the domestic legal framework specified for wetlands.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact name and year of the applicable domestic rules.
accepted.sec: Ramsar Convention - year, obligations, Montreux Record, India's sites, AP  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following treaties in chronological order of adoption or conclusion:
A. World Heritage Convention
B. IWC (Whaling Convention)
C. Ramsar Convention
D. Basel Convention
accepted.x: The IWC dates to 1946, the Ramsar Convention to 1971, the World Heritage Convention to 1972 and the Basel Convention to 1989.
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest treaties first, then resolve the middle order.
accepted.sec: Treaty → secretariat, year, India's status  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 and its Secretariat is at Bonn. The World Heritage Secretariat is in Paris, the IWC headquarters is in Cambridge, and the Basel Secretariat is in Geneva.
accepted.tq: Start with the complete treaty-year-secretariat combination and reject location swaps.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India hosted UNCCD COP-14 in 2019.
2. India ratified the World Heritage Convention in 1977.
3. India is a member of the International Whaling Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India hosted UNCCD COP-14 in 2019, ratified the World Heritage Convention in 1977 and is a member of the IWC.
accepted.tq: Combine country-status and host-country facts from different treaties.

accepted.x: The IWC Secretariat is located at Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Basel Convention is correct?
o: It concerns hazardous waste, was adopted in 1989, and entered into force in 1992.
It concerns ozone depletion and was adopted in Montreal in 1987.
It concerns wetlands and was adopted at Ramsar in 1971.
It concerns migratory species and entered into force in 1975.
accepted.x: The Basel Convention deals with hazardous waste, was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.
accepted.tq: Discriminate treaties by subject, year and commencement date.
accepted.sec: Treaty → secretariat, year, India's status  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes India's position under the Basel and Rotterdam Conventions?
o: India ratified Basel in June 1992 and acceded to Rotterdam in 2005.
India has not joined either convention.
India acceded to Basel in 2005 and ratified Rotterdam in June 1992.
accepted.x: India ratified the Basel Convention in June 1992 and acceded to the Rotterdam Convention in 2005.
accepted.tq: Separate the two treaty-status verbs and their respective years.
accepted.sec: Treaty → secretariat, year, India's status  [other exams]

accepted.s: The secretariats of the Rotterdam Convention are located at
accepted.x: The Rotterdam Convention has its Secretariat arrangements at Geneva and Rome.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired-location feature of a treaty Secretariat.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Montreal Protocol — India is a Party
accepted.x: The Montreal Protocol was adopted at Montreal in 1987, its Ozone Secretariat is at Nairobi, and India is a Party. Helsinki is not the Secretariat location.

accepted.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India is associated with an HFC freeze by
accepted.x: The Kigali-related commitment specified for India is an HFC freeze by 2028.
accepted.tq: Recall the treaty-specific target year rather than the protocol-adoption year.

Which of the following statements regarding UNCCD COP-17 is correct?
1. Its theme is “Restoring Land. Restoring Hope”.
2. The UNCCD has 197 parties.
3. Land degradation affects up to 40 per cent of land.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The stated theme, the figure of 197 parties and the estimate that land degradation affects up to 40 per cent of land are all correct.
